## TASK-001 - Freeze the implementation baseline and exact change boundaries

After separate execution authorization, refresh the TRD, source/installed/Template inventories, runtime selections, registry and mixed Git state; record exact allowed writes and preservation baselines for the implementation.

| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |

| Dependencies | None |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- A heavily modified checkout must never be reset or committed as an undifferentiated change set.
- Only separately authorized execution may begin; a ready plan or source approval supplies no mutation authority.

### Acceptance criteria

- The unchanged TRD ID/revision/hash or a newly approved successor is selected explicitly; all 30 requirements remain in scope.
- Every planned source edit, root adoption destination, generated refresh and fixture/output path has an owner and exact precondition; unrelated edits, historical evidence and state systems are protected.
- Operation-specific grants and current writers are established before affected work, including memory disposition, maintenance, guard repair and an audit-owned service probe; missing scope blocks only its dependent action.

### Planned verification

- Capture SHA256 and file metadata for protected paths and exact Git status before implementation.
- Inspect existing guards, setup/publication journals and watcher state; reconcile active owners before mutation.
- Confirm existing Python/model/package selections without provisioning and record commands and hashes.

## TASK-002 - Specify the compatible health and readiness contract

Define one documented result contract for assessed project/scope/level, required and optional selections, component detail, aggregate state and CLI compatibility within the existing ontology and memory commands.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-030 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | Verification/ontology-health-repairs/health-contract.md, SKILLS-depo/ontology/references/commands.md, SKILLS-depo/memory/references/operations.md |
| Dependencies | TASK-001 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- Treating optional disabled components as failures breaks neutral starters; treating unverified selected runtime as ready repeats F2.
- A material compatibility change beyond the TRD must return for a specific decision rather than be hidden in code.

### Acceptance criteria

- A decision table distinguishes absent/invalid request, canonical readiness, neutral setup, selected degradation, timeout, unverified runtime and intentionally disabled profiles.
- For a valid selected health request, zero means all required assessments pass; a compatible documented version/field transition preserves existing nested detail and gives callers an explicit migration.
- Observation time and relevant input identities invalidate prior readiness when dependencies change; exact field names are resolved here before implementation.

### Planned verification

- Review each audit diagnostic case against the decision table and both CLI dispatchers.
- Inspect current JSON consumers, setup receipts and tests; identify caller-visible transitions without changing Task, TRD, plan or memory-record schema by implication.

## TASK-003 - Repair source and installed fixture discovery

Replace directory-depth assumptions in reusable ontology test support with validated source/installed/Template context resolution and explicit selection of already available local runtimes.

| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |

| Dependencies | TASK-001 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- A fixture must not silently fall back to another project or copy host-specific paths into reusable assets.
- Fixture module reloading must preserve existing import isolation.

### Acceptance criteria

- Supported source, root installation, Template and initialized-project layouts resolve their own helpers/contracts at different depths and in paths with spaces.
- Temporary macOS roots are resolved before tests invoke production helpers, with production alias/symlink rejection retained.
- The standard unittest route requires no audit wrapper or import monkeypatch; unavailable optional runtimes remain explicit and never provisioned.

### Planned verification

- Run fixture discovery controls against each supported layout using disposable roots.
- Run the corrected guard cases against an explicitly selected existing standards environment and actual semantic acceptance against SYS4AI_SEMANTIC_ACCEPTANCE_ROOT.
- Retain case IDs and per-run commands; final delivered installed runs are repeated in TASK-032.

## TASK-004 - Enforce selected acceptance coverage accounting

Add a bounded verification inventory that compares required test identities with actual passes, failures, errors and explicitly permitted optional skips for the selected acceptance profile.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-007, REQ-019, REQ-020 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/ontology/tests, Verification/ontology-health-repairs/required-test-inventory.json, Verification/ontology-health-repairs/test-run-receipts |
| Dependencies | TASK-002, TASK-003 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- Aggregate test counts alone can conceal missing identities; test additions do not erase baseline obligations.

### Acceptance criteria

- The baseline 153 identities, including nine errored and 23 skipped guard cases plus one optional semantic case, are tracked without erasing the original failed discovery.
- A selected/provisioned profile with missing or unexpectedly skipped required coverage blocks acceptance; disabled optional profiles have explicit skip reasons.
- Each run retains exact command, root, runtime selection, counts, test identities, exit code and meaningful failure details.

### Planned verification

- Inject one unexpected required skip and one setup error and verify the release gate fails.
- Verify disabled optional selection is reported without pretending the skipped behavior ran.
- Compare the inventory with the original regression summary and current shipped test IDs.
